name: Schedule Management Plan
purpose: Part of the project management plan. It specifies how the project schedule will be developed, monitored and controlled: the methodology and tool, the accuracy and units of the estimates, the thresholds that trigger action, how the schedule is reported and updated, and how it links to the organization's procedures. It is developed once and does not usually change.

elements.guidance: The scheduling methodology used, whether critical path, agile or another.
The tool or tools used: scheduling software, reporting software, earned value software and so on.
The accuracy needed for estimates. It may evolve as more is known (progressive elaboration); if rolling wave planning guidelines exist, state the accuracy required as time progresses.
Whether duration estimates are in days, weeks, months or another unit.
The measures that decide whether an activity, work package or the whole project is on time, needs preventive action, or is late and needs corrective action.
The schedule information needed for status and progress reports; if a specific format is used, attach it or refer to the form or template.
The schedule outline follows the numbering structure of the WBS, and may also need to follow the organization's code of accounts or other accounting and reporting structures.
The process for updating the schedule: update frequency, permissions and version control, plus the guidelines for keeping baseline integrity and for re-baselining if necessary.

tailoring: Add the level of detail and the timing of WBS decomposition, based on rolling wave planning.
For projects that use agile, add the time box periods for releases, waves and iterations.
For projects that use earned value management, add the rules for establishing percent complete and the EVM measurement techniques (fixed formula, percent complete, level of effort and so on).
agile_or_adaptive: For projects that use agile, add information on the time box periods for releases, waves and iterations (Tailoring Tips, PDF page 67, printed page 56). Schedule methodology may be critical path, agile or another (Table 2.11, PDF page 68, printed page 57).
